trimmedBy: node trim-captures-3.2.mjs (JSON.parse, whole-record selection by position in the 10-hit page (hitsPerPage rewritten from 10 to the kept 4), regex redaction of e-mail addresses and separator-bearing phone numbers inside string values, JSON.stringify, prettier); never a byte cut
notes: search_by_date for the whoishiring account: 512 stories exist, the first page of 10 was captured, the newest 4 kept (October and September 2026, each as a "Who is hiring?" and a "Who wants to be hired?" pair). UNCLEAR: the Y Combinator terms (https://www.ycombinator.com/legal/, "Site") say "you will not engage in or use any data mining, robots, scraping or similar data gathering or extraction methods", while the HN Search API on Algolia (https://hn.algolia.com/api) is a public, unauthenticated, documented endpoint. No capture of the terms page is committed; the quote was read at that URL on 2026-10-24 and is unverifiable from this repository. Whether that API counts as "the Site" is a question for the owner, which was put to him and is unanswered, so the source stays blocked. robots.txt of news.ycombinator.com sets Crawl-delay: 30 and does not disallow /item; hn.algolia.com serves no robots.txt (404). Employers are NOT given by the API: a comment is free text whose first paragraph is a header, so every observation is tagged employer-unverified. E-mail addresses and phone numbers inside string values were replaced by a parser; personal NAMES in free-text cannot be found by a parser and were not redacted (records were chosen with short text to limit exposure).
